note: npm audit --json, run from the repo root (one npm-workspaces tree spanning backend and frontend), as of 2026-09-10: 8 vulnerable package names, all severity 'high', zero 'critical', zero 'moderate', zero 'low' (npm audit's own metadata.vulnerabilities confirms: high 8, everything else 0). All 8 trace to the SAME root cause: multer@2.2.0's advisories GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm (DoS via crafted multipart field names, high), GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf (DoS via file descriptor leak on aborted uploads, high) and GHSA-535w-7cp7-47q4 (DoS via oversized array index in field names, high) — a fourth, GHSA-qvfw-j98x-7q72 (file-size-limit bypass via async fileFilter race), is 'low' and does not appear in this baseline at all since npm audit's top-level severity for the multer entry is 'high', not 'low'. multer is pulled in by @nestjs/platform-express@11.2.3, which pins it to the EXACT version 2.2.0 (confirmed: `npm view @nestjs/platform-express@11.2.3 dependencies.multer` prints "2.2.0", no range operator) — the fix, multer 2.3.0, is not reachable without moving @nestjs/platform-express to 12.0.0 (confirmed: `npm view @nestjs/platform-express versions --json` shows 11.2.3 as the last 11.x release, followed directly by 12.0.0-alpha.0 ... 12.0.1), and `npm audit fix --dry-run` independently confirms the same thing ("To address all issues (including breaking changes), run: npm audit fix --force"). Diffing the multer 2.2.0 and 2.3.0 npm tarballs directly (`npm pack` + `diff -ru`) shows 2.3.0 is not a mechanical patch either: it changes make-middleware.js's async-context handling, adds a new fieldArrayIndexLimit option, decodes %0A/%0D/%22 out of uploaded filenames, and reworks disk.js's file-handle lifecycle around an open-stream WeakMap — real behavioural surface, not a drop-in bump. A NestJS v12 migration or an npm `overrides` pin for multer alone is out of scope for this task (porting the verify layer's audit check), so this baseline records the current, honest state rather than forcing a false green: multer itself, and every package that only 'has' this advisory because it depends (however transitively) on multer through @nestjs/core (@nestjs/platform-express, @nestjs/schedule, @nestjs/terminus, @nestjs/typeorm, nestjs-pino, and @nestjs/core itself) are ALL present in the PRODUCTION dependency tree (confirmed individually via `npm ls <name> --omit=dev` from the repo root, each returning a non-empty tree) and are therefore NOT baselined below at all — audit.mjs's hard floor fails on every one of them unconditionally, by design, and a baseline entry could not exempt them even if one were added. This repo's own media upload path (backend/src/media, up to 10MB image uploads per root CLAUDE.md) genuinely exercises multer, so this is a real, reachable advisory chain, not a false positive to be argued away. Only @nestjs/testing is dev-only (confirmed: `npm ls @nestjs/testing --omit=dev` returns an empty tree) and is the one entry recorded below. This ratchet is two-directional for whatever IS eligible for baselining: a new eligible advisory not listed here fails scripts/verify/checks/audit.mjs, and a listed entry npm audit no longer reports fails it too.

entries.name: @nestjs/testing
entries.reason: Cascades from multer@2.2.0's DoS advisories (GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm, GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf, GHSA-535w-7cp7-47q4) purely through its @nestjs/core -> @nestjs/platform-express dependency chain; npm audit lists it with no advisory of its own, only package-name 'via' entries. Confirmed dev-only: `npm ls @nestjs/testing --omit=dev` returns an empty tree, and every import of it in this repo (`grep -rl '@nestjs/testing' backend/src`) is from a *.spec.ts or *.db-spec.ts file, never from code that ships in the production bundle.
